selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Batch 32

profiles.name: Bob Chadwick
profiles.excerpt: Bob Chadwick was a recurring Escape repertory actor whose eleven surviving GRH performances document steady work in one of radio’s strongest adventure anthologies.
profiles.bio_html:
Bob Chadwick is best documented through Escape, the CBS anthology that specialized in adventure, suspense and stories of people under extreme pressure.

Personal biographical detail is limited, so his profile rests on the surviving professional record rather than unsupported identification. Repeated casting on Escape shows a dependable supporting performer able to move among new settings and characters from week to week.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Escape performances credited to Chadwick, making the series the clear center of his surviving GRH radio profile.

profiles.name: Boyd Davis
profiles.excerpt: Boyd Davis was a dependable member of the Lux Radio Theatre supporting company, heard repeatedly around major Hollywood stars in feature-film adaptations.
profiles.bio_html:
Boyd Davis worked in the professional supporting repertory used by Lux Radio Theatre. The series brought major film stars to the microphone but depended on experienced stock actors to fill the many smaller roles required by each adaptation.

Surviving cast records place Davis in productions such as Practically Yours, A Tale of Two Cities and other Lux broadcasts. His repeated presence reflects the practical craft of a radio utility actor rather than celebrity billing.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Davis, documenting his place in the program's regular supporting company.

profiles.name: Charles Maxwell
profiles.excerpt: Charles Maxwell was a West Coast radio character actor whose surviving GRH work is concentrated in This Is Your FBI.
profiles.bio_html:
Charles Maxwell worked in the West Coast radio repertory during the postwar years, appearing in crime and dramatic programs that relied on experienced supporting actors.

This Is Your FBI became the strongest concentration of his surviving GRH work. The series dramatized criminal investigations in a documentary-influenced style, and Maxwell returned repeatedly in changing supporting roles.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 This Is Your FBI performances credited to Maxwell, providing a focused record of his radio character work.

profiles.name: Claire Verdera
profiles.excerpt: Claire Verdera was a recurring Lux Radio Theatre supporting actress whose eleven surviving GRH performances place her inside the program’s Hollywood stock company.
profiles.bio_html:
Claire Verdera worked in the supporting company of Lux Radio Theatre, where weekly adaptations of major films required a deep bench of actors around the featured stars.

Surviving scripts and cast lists place Verdera in productions including Mrs. Moonlight, Suspicion and The Canterville Ghost. Her repeated assignments show the kind of reliable stock work that made the large-scale broadcasts possible.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Verdera, documenting a concentrated body of professional radio work.

profiles.name: Florence Ravenel
profiles.excerpt: Florence Ravenel built a long stage, radio and screen career, including major daytime-radio work before later television roles.
profiles.bio_html:
Florence Ravenel was born in Michigan in 1896 and trained at Hunter College and the Neighborhood Playhouse. Her professional career stretched from the stage into radio, film and television.

Radio became a major part of that career, including work on The Court of Missing Heirs and other dramatic programs. She later continued as a character actress on television, including The Farmer's Daughter.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six NBC University Theater performances credited under the source spelling Florence Ravenal, three Let George Do It appearances and additional work on Broadway Is My Beat and Dr. Kildare. Her public profile uses the canonical spelling Florence Ravenel.

profiles.name: Hester Sondergaard
profiles.excerpt: Hester Sondergaard was a stage and radio actress known for exceptional command of dialects and for helping organize The American School of the Air.
profiles.bio_html:
Hester Sondergaard was born in Minnesota in 1903, studied at the University of Minnesota and entered professional theatre in the 1920s. She was the sister of actress Gale Sondergaard but developed a substantial career of her own.

Radio became one of Hester Sondergaard's strongest professional arenas. She helped organize The American School of the Air, worked in serials including Portia Faces Life and Road of Life, and was noted for command of numerous accents and dialects.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five Columbia Workshop performances credited to Sondergaard, three Words at War appearances and additional work on 2000 Plus, Cloak and Dagger and The Mysterious Traveler.

profiles.name: Hugh Studebaker
profiles.excerpt: Hugh Studebaker spent decades in radio as actor, announcer and pianist, with continuing roles ranging from Silly Watson to major daytime serial characters.
profiles.bio_html:
Hugh Studebaker was born in Indiana in 1900 and entered broadcasting first as a pianist before becoming a radio actor in the early 1930s. He developed into one of the medium's durable character performers.

Studebaker played Silly Watson on Fibber McGee and Molly and held continuing roles on programs including Bachelor's Children, The Guiding Light and The Right to Happiness. He also worked professionally as an announcer, including years with Ted Malone's Between the Bookends.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Fibber McGee and Molly performances credited to Studebaker. His announcing and early professional piano work remain part of his public classification alongside acting.

profiles.name: Jack Edwards Jr.
profiles.excerpt: Jack Edwards Jr. grew up in a radio-performing family and built a career as actor, singer and producer before later voice work in animation.
profiles.bio_html:
Jack Edwards Jr. was born into a performing family and was placed onstage while still an infant. With his brother Sam Edwards, he became a familiar young radio performer through family and juvenile programs during the 1930s.

Edwards continued as a radio actor and singer into adulthood and later headed his own radio-packaging operation, giving production a real place in his career. He also worked in film, television and animation voice acting.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three Encore Theater performances credited to Edwards, two each on Escape and Lux Radio Theatre, and additional work across comedy, suspense and anthology programs.

profiles.name: James Van Dyk
profiles.excerpt: James Van Dyk was a New York radio repertory actor heard repeatedly in Quiet Please, The Mysterious Traveler and other supernatural and mystery anthologies.
profiles.bio_html:
James Van Dyk belongs to the New York radio repertory whose work survives more clearly in broadcasts than in later personal biography.

Van Dyk appeared repeatedly on Quiet, Please and The Mysterious Traveler, including early Quiet, Please productions written and directed by Wyllis Cooper. His other credits placed him in mystery, horror and dramatic anthology.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three performances each on Quiet, Please and The Mysterious Traveler credited to Van Dyk, plus appearances on Dr. Christian, Molle Mystery Theatre, The Shadow and The Weird Circle.

profiles.name: John Thomas
profiles.excerpt: John Thomas was a New York radio repertory actor whose surviving work is strongest in X Minus One and later network drama.
profiles.bio_html:
John Thomas is best documented through the surviving New York radio repertory of the 1940s and 1950s. Personal biographical detail is limited, so the professional broadcast record remains the strongest basis for his profile.

Thomas appeared repeatedly on X Minus One and also worked on The Chase, Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, Stroke of Fate and Words at War. Those credits place him across science fiction, crime and wartime anthology drama.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five X Minus One performances credited to Thomas, two each on The Chase and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, and additional anthology work.
